rootCause: SkillMatchController.skillMatch (src/modules/skills/presentation/skills.controller.ts:140-146) reads the `skills` query param as a plain string and immediately calls `skills.split(',')` (line 144) with no validation. The param is declared `@ApiQuery({ name: 'skills', required: true })` but there is NO ValidationPipe/DefaultValuePipe/required check enforcing it at runtime. When the `skills` query param is OMITTED entirely, `skills` is `undefined`, so `undefined.split(',')` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')`, which Nest maps to HTTP 500. This is a missing-input-validation defect: a missing REQUIRED param should yield 400, not 500. It is NOT reachable from the UI (see uiCaller). Note: an empty value `skills=` does NOT crash ("".split gives ['' ] which is filtered to [] -> service returns [] -> 200). This is one instance of a systemic pattern on staging — the same missing-query-param .split/.match crash also fires on /api/my-time/month, /api/my-time/gaps, /api/time-management/team-calendar, /api/time-management/compliance (observed in same log window; out of scope for this slice).

suggestedFix: Make the missing-param case yield 400 instead of 500. Minimal fix: change the controller signature to validate/normalize before split, e.g. `@Query('skills') skills?: string` and `if (!skills) throw new BadRequestException('skills query param is required');` before splitting (BadRequestException is already imported in this file). Cleaner: introduce a query DTO with `@IsString() @IsNotEmpty() skills: string` and bind a ValidationPipe. SEPARATE correctness bug (not a 500, do NOT block on it here): the UI sends skill publicIds (skl_…, since listSkills() returns id=publicId) but skills.service.skillMatch queries `personSkill.findMany({ where: { skillId: { in: skillIds } } })` against the raw UUID column with no publicId→uuid translation, so realistic UI inputs always return [] — the endpoint silently never matches anyone. Worth filing separately.
uiCaller: frontend/src/lib/api/skills.ts → fetchSkillMatch(skillIds, projectId) builds `?skills=<ids.join(',')>&projectId=<id>` and ALWAYS sets the `skills` param. Sole consumer is frontend/src/components/assignments/SkillMatchPanel.tsx (handleSearch, line 61), which early-returns when selectedSkillIds.length === 0, so it never issues a param-less request. CRITICAL: SkillMatchPanel is ORPHANED — grep finds zero imports/mounts of it anywhere in the frontend, so this endpoint has no live UI surface. The param-less 500 is unreachable through the app; it only occurs on a manual/QA probe that omits `skills`.
